Mutations in PHKA1 (GSD IXd) and PHKG2 (GSD IXc) impair the activity of the phosphorylase kinase complex, which is essential for activating glycogen phosphorylase. This leads to a reduction in glycogenolysis, resulting in the accumulation of glycogen and impaired glucose production, manifesting as hepatomegaly and hypoglycemia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in PHKA1 or PHKG2 who do not exhibit hepatomegaly or hypoglycemia, or demonstration that mutations in these genes do not impair phosphorylase kinase activity. _(variant: gnomad v2.1.1 shows very low allele frequencies for pathogenic variants in PHKA1 and PHKG2, consistent with rare disease-causing variants.)_
